definition: To finger someone; to digitally stimulate a partner's genitals, or for a woman to digitally stimulate her own genitalia.
notes: Literally 'to do it with the finger'; applies to both self and partner stimulation depending on context; placed in the masturbation section by convention but frequently transitive.

definition: To touch or move oneself; a highly context-dependent euphemistic verb for masturbation.
notes: Literally 'to move oneself'; the sexual meaning requires heavy contextual support; the dominant everyday use means 'to hurry up' or 'to get moving.'

definition: To rub oneself; slang for masturbation, particularly associated with female self-stimulation through friction.
notes: Literally 'to rub oneself'; friction-based framing makes it more commonly associated with vulvar/clitoral rubbing than penetrative self-stimulation; non-sexual uses (towel-drying, chafing) coexist.

definition: Anal sex; the standard Brazilian Portuguese term for any sexual act involving penetration of the anus.
Anal; shorthand for anal sex, widely used in casual speech, internet contexts, and pornographic taxonomy.
To put it in the ass; crude expression for performing insertive anal sex.
english_term: to put it up the ass
notes: 'Cu' is the dominant crude Brazilian Portuguese word for anus; 'colocar' (to place/put) is milder than 'meter' but the phrase overall is unambiguously crude.

definition: To stick it in the ass; crude slang for insertive anal penetration.
english_term: to stick it up the ass
notes: 'Meter' is a high-frequency crude verb for penetration in Brazilian Portuguese; slightly more aggressive in tone than 'colocar no cu.'

definition: To give up one's ass; crude expression specifying the receptive role in anal sex.
english_term: to take it up the ass
notes: Literally 'to give the ass'; the 'giving' framing specifies passivity; heavily used as an insult implying weakness, submission, or defeat far beyond sexual contexts.

definition: To take it in the ass; crude expression for the receptive role in anal sex.
english_term: to take it up the ass
notes: Also used figuratively to mean suffering a serious setback or being badly cheated ('tomei no cu nessa negociação' = 'I got royally screwed in that deal').

definition: To sodomize; to anally penetrate someone; a verb derived from 'rabo' (tail/buttocks).
notes: Derived from 'rabo' (ass/tail); implies insertive anal penetration; somewhat more dated or regional than phrases built on 'cu'; also appears as a metaphor for cheating someone.

definition: To shove it in the hole; crude expression for anal penetration, occasionally ambiguous with vaginal penetration.
english_term: to shove it in the hole
notes: 'Buraco' (hole) defaults to the anus in sexual context; some regional usage extends 'buraco' to the vagina, creating occasional ambiguity.

definition: To do it through the back end; a crude-euphemistic expression for anal sex using 'fundilho' (trouser seat/crotch seam) as a metonym for the anus.
english_term: to do it through the back door
notes: 'Fundilho' refers to the seat/crotch seam of pants; lower recognition among younger speakers for whom 'fundilho' itself is unfamiliar vocabulary.

definition: To break open; to forcefully and roughly penetrate anally, implying tearing or extreme dilation.
notes: Literally 'to break down a door'; in sexual use implies violent or rough anal penetration to the point of injury; also an all-purpose Brazilian expletive and metaphor for defeating someone decisively.

definition: Sperm or semen; the standard semi-clinical term used in everyday speech and sex education in Brazil.
notes: In Brazilian Portuguese, 'esperma' is used interchangeably for both individual spermatozoa and bulk semen fluid, collapsing the English distinction; appears in health curricula and mainstream media without censorship.

definition: Semen; the strictly clinical anatomical term for the fluid ejaculated at orgasm.
notes: The circumflex accent (sêmen) was orthographically required pre-2009 Acordo Ortográfico; post-reform the accent was dropped in Brazil, so both spellings appear in texts; more formal than 'esperma.'

definition: Ejaculate; the fluid expelled at orgasm; a nominalized past participle of 'ejacular.'
notes: Less commonly used as a standalone noun than 'esperma' or 'sêmen'; more natural in clinical writing than in speech; the verb form 'ejaculou' (he/she ejaculated) is more frequently encountered.

definition: Cum; semen; and simultaneously the most ubiquitous Brazilian Portuguese expletive, roughly equivalent to 'fuck' or 'damn.'
notes: Historically denoted semen; now functions primarily as an all-purpose expletive with near-universal recognition across all age groups and socioeconomic strata; the semen meaning is retained only in explicitly sexual contexts.

definition: Little milk; an affectionate or playful diminutive euphemism for semen.
notes: Diminutive of 'leite' (milk); the '-inho' suffix adds cuteness or intimacy, making it noticeably less crude than 'porra'; common in flirtatious texting and softcore pornographic contexts.

definition: Milk; a euphemism for semen exploiting the visual and textural resemblance to cow's milk.
notes: Primary meaning (dairy milk) vastly dominates in neutral contexts; sexual meaning is activated only by surrounding context; common in pornographic dialogue and internet sexual slang.

definition: Orgasm; climax; the noun form of 'gozar,' the standard colloquial verb for reaching orgasm in Brazil.
notes: 'Gozar' and 'gozo' are culturally more neutral in Brazil than 'cum' is in English — used freely in song lyrics and mainstream media; the word can secondarily refer to the ejaculate itself.

definition: A load; a cumshot; an event noun denoting the act of orgasming or the ejaculate expelled.
notes: Feminine noun derived from 'gozar'; can denote the orgasmic event or the ejaculate as a product; more graphic and event-focused than 'gozo'; widely used in pornographic description.

definition: Vaginal secretion; the clinical term for any fluid produced by the vagina, whether arousal-related or pathological.
Lubrication; the clinical term for vaginal wetness produced during sexual arousal.
Wet; colloquial adjective describing a woman as sexually aroused and producing vaginal lubrication.
notes: Adjective with feminine gender agreement; sexual meaning requires context — base word is generic; 'estar molhada' = to be wet/aroused.

definition: To get wet; the inchoative colloquial phrase for a woman becoming sexually aroused and producing vaginal lubrication.
notes: The stative-change verb 'ficar' (to become/to get) combines with 'molhada' to mark the onset of arousal rather than a static state; used in first-person self-report and third-person description alike.
